clue.text: On right, with fixed agenda, no Democrat!

definitions.text: On right, with fixed agenda, no Democrat!

indicators.note: fixed in the sense of rigged or doctored, so the remaining letters are rearranged
no here means the letter standing for Democrat is taken away from agenda

parts.note: D is the usual abbreviation for a Democrat in US politics

explanation.surface: A rallying cry for a right-winger with a settled programme and no time for the other party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' drops D, and 'fixed' rearranges what is left of agenda into EAGAN. Read whole, the clue also describes the man: a Republican, on the right, set in his programme.
explanation.definitionFit: Ronald Reagan was a Republican US president, a right-winger and so by definition not of the Democratic party.

clue.text: Insurrection's steady rise over time

indicators.note: in a down clue, over puts the first piece on top of the next
in a down clue, rise means the word is read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: a steady is a regular boyfriend or girlfriend, a lover

explanation.surface: A news line about a rebellion that keeps building gradually over a period.
explanation.walkthrough: 'steady' looks like an adjective for the rise, but it is a noun: someone you are going steady with. 'rise' turns that word upwards to REVOL.
explanation.definitionFit: A revolt is an uprising against authority, which is what an insurrection is.

clue.text: Caught in sort of calculating behaviour that's hard to stop

indicators.note: in tells us the abbreviation for caught is placed inside the other piece

parts.note: addition is one kind of arithmetic calculation
C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

explanation.surface: Someone trapped in a compulsive habit of number-crunching that they cannot break.
explanation.definitionFit: An addiction is a compulsive habit, a dependence one struggles to give up.

clue.text: Share out about fifty tons

indicators.note: about means going round, so one piece is put inside the other

parts.note: tons, informally, means a great deal: a lot
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: Dividing up roughly fifty tons of goods between people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' looks like 'approximately' before fifty, but it is the container signal: A LOT goes round L.
explanation.definitionFit: To allot is to distribute or apportion shares among people.

clue.text: Labour leader, with 40 per cent cut, is making a bloomer

indicators.note: losing forty per cent of the leader's ten-letter name means keeping only its opening six letters

parts.note: Clem Attlee, Labour Party leader and post-war British prime minister, was always known as Clem
taken as written

explanation.surface: A Labour leader whose budget has been slashed is about to make a blunder.
explanation.walkthrough: Clement Attlee led Britain's Labour Party and was Prime Minister 1945-51. 'with 40 per cent cut' keeps CLEMAT, six of the ten letters of CLEM ATTLEE. 'bloomer' looks like a mistake but means a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: The clematis is a climbing plant grown for its flowers, so it is something that blooms.

clue.text: Autobiography of chicken? It's appearing in instalments

explanation.surface: A comic idea of a farmyard bird writing its life story in serial parts.
explanation.walkthrough: Chicken Little is the fable chick who thinks the sky is falling, so the life story of Chicken Little could be titled with its own surname twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means gradually, a bit at a time, and the first part jokes that Chicken Little's memoir would be by Little himself.

clue.text: Is much excited by total theatre of a sort

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so these letters are thrown into a new order

parts.note: total, as in the whole lot, means all

explanation.surface: A theatre that becomes thrilling when everything comes together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'excited' rearranges IS MUCH into MUSICH.
explanation.definitionFit: A music hall is a type of theatre staging variety entertainment, popular in Victorian Britain.

clue.text: Chest containing ton, approximately

parts.note: 'or so' means roughly, approximately

explanation.surface: A storage chest holding about a ton.
explanation.walkthrough: 'containing' tempts a container reading, but it only links the definition to the wordplay; T is followed by OR SO.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the trunk of the body, including the chest.

clue.text: Sluggish male new worker succeeds

indicators.note: succeeds means comes after, so the worker goes at the end

parts.note: a stag is a male deer, and a stag party is men only
the ant is the crossword's stock worker

explanation.surface: A slow man is replaced by a newly hired employee.
explanation.definitionFit: Stagnant water does not flow, so the word means sluggish or inactive.

clue.text: Part of leg badly beset by pains — nurse operating

indicators.note: beset by means surrounded by, so the first piece goes inside the second

parts.note: pains are aches
badly, as in poorly, means ill
to nurse is to tend
operating, as in working, means on

explanation.surface: A leg injury that hurts badly while a nurse is at work on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'operating' suggests surgery but just means switched on; 'beset by' sets one synonym inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The Achilles tendon joins the calf muscles to the heel bone at the back of the lower leg.

clue.text: Namely, elicited reforms with small volume

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for volume, the small form of the word

indicators.note: reforms means shapes again, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A formal note that the evidence gathered was rewritten in a slim book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reforms' rearranges the letters of elicited into IDELICET. 'Namely' is the English sense of the Latin word abbreviated viz.
explanation.definitionFit: Videlicet is Latin for 'that is to say', abbreviated viz.

clue.text: Country featured in fairy story from east

indicators.note: in an across clue, from east means read right to left, backwards
featured in says the answer sits inside the clue's words, across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A land that appears in a fairy tale told from the Orient.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Country featured' as the definition, but 'featured in' is the hidden-word signal, so the definition is 'Country' alone. AIRYS sits inside FAIRY STORY and 'from east' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Syria is a nation in the Middle East.

clue.text: Stated need for a large number of Indians

indicators.note: stated means said out loud, so we want a word sounding like another

parts.note: a need is a lack of something

explanation.surface: A claim that a great many Indian people are in want.
explanation.walkthrough: A lac (or lakh) is the Indian term for one hundred thousand, so it is a large number used by Indians.
explanation.definitionFit: In India and South Asia a lac is the unit for one hundred thousand, especially of rupees.

clue.text: Headgear of pope that went to Ireland again this year

definitions.text: that went to Ireland again this year

explanation.surface: Papal headwear that seems to have travelled to Ireland once more.
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby Triple Crown is won by the home nation (England, Scotland, Wales or Ireland) that beats the other three in the Six Nations; Ireland won it in 2006 and 2007.
explanation.definitionFit: The papal tiara has three tiers, and the rugby trophy is for beating all three other home nations.

clue.text: Not noise that's noteworthy

explanation.surface: Telling apart a meaningful message from mere noise.
explanation.walkthrough: In electronics and communication the meaningful part of a transmission is contrasted with the noise around it; as an adjective the word means striking or notable, as in a signal victory.
explanation.definitionFit: The wanted transmission is what engineers contrast with interference, and as an adjective it means remarkable, as in a signal success.

clue.text: Awfully tinny note not even second fiddle produced

indicators.note: awfully, as in badly done, means these letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A violinist plays a poor thin note and is not even good enough for second fiddle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Awfully' rearranges TINNY NOTE. 'Second fiddle' is someone of minor importance, so a person who is not even that is a nobody.
explanation.definitionFit: A nonentity is a person of no importance at all, lower even than someone playing a subordinate role.

clue.text: Priest at home with singular composer?

indicators.note: singular means the name is treated as a plural and its final S is dropped

parts.note: Johannes Brahms was the German Romantic composer
at home means in

explanation.surface: A clergyman relaxing at home with a remarkable composer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'singular' looks like 'remarkable', but it makes BRAHMS singular by dropping its S. The charade is in answer order: BRAHM then IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A Brahmin is a member of the Hindu priestly caste.

clue.text: He announced storm at sea, danger to shipping

indicators.note: announced means spoken aloud, so we write a word that sounds the same

parts.note: he refers to a male

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A weather forecaster warns that a storm out at sea threatens ships.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' sounds like MALE, written MAEL; 'at sea' rearranges STORM into STROM.
explanation.definitionFit: A maelstrom is a powerful whirlpool, which can drag down vessels.

clue.text: Calculating devices accountant used in corruption

indicators.note: used in means put into the following word

parts.note: corruption, as in misuse or wrongdoing, means abuses
AC, as in a/c, is a short form for account, here standing for accountant

explanation.surface: Counting frames that a crooked bookkeeper put to fraudulent use.
explanation.walkthrough: 'used in' splits the synonym for corruption after its second letter to take the short form of accountant.
explanation.definitionFit: An abacus is a frame with beads on rods used for counting, the earliest calculating tool.

clue.text: Fruit and nuts

explanation.surface: Two bits of produce side by side on a market stall.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense is slang: nuts means crazy, and so does the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A long curved yellow tropical fruit, and informal for mad or crazy.

clue.text: In the 50s, university education settled down

indicators.note: In means the next piece is placed inside the fifties

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for fifty, so several fifties are several Ls

explanation.surface: In the 1950s a university education helped someone settle into life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the 50s' looks like a decade but is plural Roman numerals: U goes in among the Ls.
explanation.definitionFit: Lulled means calmed or soothed into quiet, settled down.

clue.text: Film of book, sequel to first one

explanation.surface: A movie adaptation that follows on from an opening story.
explanation.walkthrough: The 1960 film was made from Leon Uris's novel; the Bible's second book follows Genesis.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a film adapted from a novel, and the second book of the Old Testament, following Genesis.

clue.text: Fraudulent scheme to place restraint on tenant

parts.note: a chain is a restraint
a letter is one who lets property, the tenant's counterpart

explanation.surface: A dodgy plan to impose restrictions on someone renting a property.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain letter asks each recipient to send copies on, often promising money, and is a common swindle.

clue.text: Cancel woman's university lecture at the start

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name

indicators.note: at the start means we take only the opening letter of lecture

explanation.surface: A woman calls off her university lecture right at the beginning.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul is to declare void or invalid, to cancel.

clue.text: Black pig

explanation.surface: A dark-coloured pig.
explanation.walkthrough: As a verb the answer means to eat greedily, so to pig; as an adjective it means glossy black, like the bird.
explanation.definitionFit: Glossy black like the bird's plumage, and to devour greedily as a glutton does.

clue.text: Lots of cricketers backed a larger boundary

indicators.note: backed means the word is turned round, read from the back

parts.note: a cricket team is an XI, so several teams are XIs

explanation.surface: Cricket teams supporting a bigger playing area.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket a ball hit over the boundary rope without bouncing scores six runs, more than the four for one that bounces first.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket the six is the bigger of the two boundary scores, beating a four.

clue.text: Sloth after sloth, perhaps, seen in desert area

indicators.note: after places the animal behind the sin

parts.note: sloth is one of the seven deadly sins, so it is an example of a sin
the ai is a three-toed sloth

explanation.surface: One slow animal following another across a desert.
explanation.walkthrough: The capitalised 'Sloth' is the animal AI; 'sloth, perhaps' is the deadly sin.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sinai is the peninsula of desert between Egypt and Israel.

clue.text: Produced new issue sent to the house

explanation.surface: A magazine's latest number is printed and posted out to homes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' is offspring: a mother who has given birth is said to have been delivered of a baby.
explanation.definitionFit: To give birth, bringing offspring into the world, and to bring goods or post to someone's door.

clue.text: Son making friends and going out

parts.note: allying means joining forces, making friends

explanation.surface: A boy who is out socialising and making new friends.
explanation.definitionFit: Sallying means setting out or venturing forth.

clue.text: Bad feeling a game with America produces

parts.note: nim is a game of taking objects from heaps
US is short for United States, America

explanation.surface: Playing a game against the Americans leaves resentment.
explanation.definitionFit: Animus means hostility or ill will.
